This is a reminder that an automated footprint scan is only as complete as its own coverage-detection logic (which, as seen with the Uber and 400/410 China Basin false positives, can both over- and under-report); a direct visual spot-check against satellite imagery remains the most reliable verification and should have been part of the original reconciliation claim, not a follow-up prompted by the owner catching it.

column5: Second correction pass: a real-block coverage audit found 9 under-tracked blocks, fixed a geometry bug and added two new real records.
column6: SECOND correction pass on Mission Bay coverage claims, this time using a proper method: rather than eyeballing footprints, polygonized real city blocks from real street geometry (src/block_fit.py's load_blocks(), the same tool used elsewhere in this project to fit new features against real blocks) and computed, for every real block touching the Mission Bay boundary, what fraction of its actual building footprint area is covered by a tracked record. Of 58 real blocks with >=30% of their area inside the boundary, 33 have meaningful real building coverage (>3% of block area built); this audit found 9 of those 33 were under 50% tracked. Investigated all 9: fixed a real bug in 500 Terry A. Francois Boulevard's own geometry (mission_bay_500_terry_francois.geojson) -- it had only ever captured 1 of 3 real DataSF footprint pieces sharing its mblr (the smallest, ~1172 sq m, missing ~7460 sq m of the real ~8636 sq m building), now corrected to the union of all 3; added 1401 Third Street (an office building, built 2009, about 222,000 sq ft, both per the Assessor roll; tenant not identified) and the Chase Center Parking Garage (150 Warriors Way, built 2009; 469,726 sq ft per a Redfin listing, not a primary source) as new real records. Four blocks remain under 50% tracked: all are minor (building footprint under 17% of their block's area) with no address found in DataSF Assessor parcel data to identify them -- left undocumented rather than guessed, same treatment as the already-investigated 'Community Center Garage' fragment near the Rutter Community Center. This audit method (real polygonized blocks + building-footprint coverage fraction) is more rigorous than the ad hoc satellite spot-checks and footprint-distance scans used in the prior two passes and should be the standard going forward for any future Mission Bay completeness claim.

This is a reminder that the real-block coverage-fraction audit method (comparing DataSF building footprints against tracked geometry) can itself under-report coverage when a real building's Assessor parcel boundary and its DataSF building-footprint outline don't line up exactly -- it found a genuine gap here, but also one false positive, and both needed the same tax-roll cross-check to resolve either way.

column6: Mission Bay Block 6E real-parcel find, prompted by the owner directly asking why the map only showed 7E and not 7W. Investigating that pushed a re-check of the plan-to-real-world transform's local accuracy: the label positions for 7E and 7W (fit from 6 control points clustered in the South campus core) drift enough this far out that the 7W label position actually lands inside a different, adjacent block's building -- 1300 Fourth Street (Mission Bay South Block 6 East), a 142-unit TNDC affordable housing development (plus a manager's unit, mid-block mews of 12 townhomes/10 flats, groundbreaking anticipated in 2016 per SocketSite's Aug 2016 'about to break ground' item) that was genuinely untracked. Added as a real status.csv row, not an approximate trace. This is a concrete instance of the known limitation already logged for the PDF-transform approach: label positions this far from the control-point cluster cannot be trusted for identifying which real building a plan label refers to without an independent check (here, the DataSF Assessor tax-roll API) -- exactly the caveat under which the transform was adopted in the first place.

column6: Verified a second research batch covering the 16 records this project had deliberately left undated (docs/briefs/research-verification-2.md). column6: Verified a third research batch (docs/briefs/research-verification-3.md), following ground rules the project gave it after two earlier rounds. Citations were real and quotable far more often this time, but two of the 13 claims were still rejected before verification even started -- both cited real documents describing a different physical parcel than this project tracks (Block 22 vs. Bayfront Park/P22, confirmed ~500m apart and matching UCSF's own "Koret Quad" label; the P26 interchange wedge vs. the real, separately-named Mariposa Park, confirmed via San Francisco's own Legistar API that the cited ordinance's own title places it on a different street). column5: Split Chase Center's shared parcel from Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4; merged Harmonic Brewing's building in.
column6: The owner identified that DataSF's Assessor Parcel dataset gives Chase Center (formerly tracked as status.csv blklot 8722025) and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (formerly blklot 8722063) byte-identical geometry -- one shared master-condominium-association land parcel spanning the whole Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32 superblock (confirmed: Chase Center, both Uber towers, a parking structure and a small broadcast building are all separate condo units on one shared plat). column5: Added 36 of our own street-level photos of 19 Mission Bay records, taken on Sept. 23 and 24, 2026.
column6: First batch of Pier & Point's own photographs, taken by Pierre Rohel on a walk through Mission Bay North and South on 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 and published under CC BY 4.0 with the credit 'Pierre Rohel / Pier & Point'. Each photo was placed on its record by the photographer on site. The hosted copies are resized and upright, with licence plates and recognisable faces blurred and all camera metadata removed except the credit and license. Nine of the 19 records had no record file before; each now has a minimal one carrying only what this project already recorded about it. Three more photos (rowhouses at 113-117 Berry St and the Mission Creek Senior Community at about 225 Berry St) are held back: neither building is tracked here yet.

column5: Added a nearby-project record for the Piers 68 & 70 dry docks, next to Pier 70 but outside its tracked boundary.
column6: New adjacent record for the Piers 68 & 70 dry docks (Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock), following the Port's December 2025 emergency declaration over Dry Dock No. 2's hull tears and listing, the January and February 2026 Port/Capital Planning Committee memos on stabilization and planned demolition, and Mission Local's February 2026 reporting on the $61.2M disposal cost.

column5: Added a nearby-project record for Pier 54, condemned in 2024 and now partly funded for demolition.
column6: New adjacent record for Pier 54, closed and red-tagged in 2024 (SFGate), with the Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) budgeting $2.0M to demolish the pier shed across FY2026-27 and FY2027-28.

column5: Added a nearby-project record for the Mission Bay Ferry Landing, under construction near Agua Vista Park.
column6: New adjacent record for the WETA/Port Mission Bay Ferry Landing, near Agua Vista Park on Terry A. Francois Blvd, targeted for completion by the end of 2027, with SFCTA approving further Prop L sales-tax funding toward it in April 2026.

column5: UCSF bought 409 and 499 Illinois St for $767 million to build its new School of Dentistry.
column6: UC Regents bought 409 Illinois St and 499 Illinois St together from Alexandria Real Estate Equities for $767,000,000 (closed 2025-12-17), and is renovating 409 Illinois St (261,117 sq ft) into a new School of Dentistry and Interprofessional Education Center with Suffolk and CO Architects, targeted to open in late 2029.

column5: Added a nearby-project record for 700 Indiana St, a proposed Dogpatch lab building next to Pier 70.
column6: New adjacent record for 700 Indiana St, a proposed lab/office building for MBC BioLabs approved by the Planning Commission in June 2024, with a neighborhood CEQA appeal rejected by the Board of Supervisors in September 2024.

column5: Added a nearby-project record for Piers 38 and 40, a stalled-then-revived redevelopment next to Mission Rock.
column6: New adjacent record for Piers 38 & 40, whose original 2021 Exclusive Negotiating Agreement lapsed in 2023; the Port Commission settled a related back-rent dispute and adopted an Amended and Restated ENA with a 12-month evaluation period in April 2026.

column5: Added a nearby-project record for the 22nd St Caltrain station's ADA accessibility retrofit.
column6: New adjacent record for the 22nd Street Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement, funded in part by SFCTA Prop L and a September 2026 FTA All Stations Accessibility Program grant.

column5: Corrected Mission Bay School's cost, completion, opening-date and background details to match its cited sources.
column6: The record now gives the construction contract as about $95.4 million (SF Standard, Aug 2026) instead of $95,390,000, and says SFUSD scheduled construction to finish by January 2026 rather than stating that it was completed. The first day of school is shown as August 2026, since the readable sources give only the month. The 2022 UCSF site transfer and 1988 set-aside, the Multistudio architect credit, the Architecture 2030 claim, the attendee list at the 2022 groundbreaking and the 'first new school in 20 years' wording were removed or corrected because no cited source supports them. Sources were added for the design-build team, the Proposition A bond and the fourth-floor program.

column5: Corrected Five88's unit count, groundbreaking wording, tenant permit rows and image credits to match their sources.
column6: The record now says 200 affordable apartments as SocketSite reported them (not '198 plus a manager's unit') and treats SocketSite's January 2015 piece as a forecast of an April 2015 groundbreaking, not a report that it happened; the 'under construction' milestone was removed. Changelog rows that said Blue Bottle Coffee was announced, and that Proper Foods and Bank of America opened, were reworded to say only that a sign permit exists. Rows about the teller-line, address-correction, excavation and sliding-door permits now say what the DBI permit rows show (issued or completed, and which permit). The Assessor note now reflects the 2023-2025 rolls (year built 2017, 208 units), the NAIP credit names the Farm Production and Conservation Business Center, and the Wikimedia credit no longer names an author or a flight that the file page does not state.

column5: Corrected 1300 Fourth Street's groundbreaking, developer, retail-tenant and schedule wording to match its sources.
column6: SocketSite's August 2016 piece is now described as a forecast that construction would start in late September 2016, not a report that groundbreaking happened, and the 'under construction' milestone was removed. TNDC is described as the owner per Ventura Partners and as the units' manager per SocketSite, not as developer, and Ventura Partners is called the commercial property manager. Happy Lemon and SomiSomi now show no opening date, because a DataSF business registration does not show that a storefront opened, and their changelog rows were reworded the same way. The OCII rows now say an option to ground lease was authorized, give the 34 resident and 5 commercial parking spaces without our own 39 total, and no longer attach the 2019 completion to a 2016 schedule. Status notes cite Ventura Partners for the 2019 completion, and the Wikimedia credit no longer names an author or a flight the file page does not state.

column5: Corrected 490/499 Illinois Street's sizes, names and ownership wording, and flagged the unresolved 490 versus 499 footprint.
column6: The record no longer says 499 Illinois is about 450,000 sq ft (SGH gives a 500,000 sq ft center in two buildings; SF Standard gives 470,000 sq ft for 409 and 499 together), calls the 490 Illinois buildings separate rather than connected as SF YIMBY says, cites the 2006 DBI permit for six stories, and no longer names Alexandria as developer (a 2013 Alexandria release and SF Standard show ownership only) or the 490 building's developer as UCSF (SF YIMBY says only that it opened for UCSF). The Vision Center's November 2020 opening is now stated as SF YIMBY's report on November 27, 2020, without a stated opening day. The map label no longer uses the name 'Alexandria Center for Science and Technology', which no cited source uses for 499 Illinois. UCSF's lease and purchase at 499 Illinois is now cited to SF Standard (Dec 2025) and the reproductive health clinic to UCSF Health's location page. A dated note in digitization_method records that OpenStreetMap labels the two ways the opposite of this file's assignment and that DataSF parcels show a 409/499 pairing; which footprint is 490 Illinois is left to the owner. The Wikimedia credit no longer names an author or a flight the file page does not state.

column5: Corrected Genentech Hall's campus size, programs, architect office, parcel figures and image date to match their sources.
column6: The '303-acre campus' wording was dropped (that is the whole Mission Bay area; UCSF's history and Clark describe a 43-acre campus), the programs housed now follow UCSF's history page (structural and chemical biology, molecular, cell and developmental biology, the Molecular Design Institute) rather than 'biochemistry, biophysics', and the unsupported 'San Francisco office' for SmithGroup was removed. Size and story-count facts now also cite UCSF's history and Clark. The parcel caveat now gives 675 Mission Bay Blvd at about 12.2 acres, and a dated note says the tax-roll claim for 600 16th St is unsupported (the parcel is addressed 1700 4th St). The Block 24A/B label now cites UCSF's June 2025 CAC map. The 2008 photo no longer carries a 'taken' date because the source dates only the presentation, and the Wikimedia credit no longer names an author or a flight the file page does not state. The January 2003 opening and 'first building' claims rest on a Tradeline article that could not be read and were left in place.

column5: Removed Mission Hall's unsupported seven-story and Office of the Chancellor claims and fixed its size, address and credit wording.
column6: No readable source gives a story count (OpenStreetMap tags six levels) or names the Office of the Chancellor as an occupant, so 'seven-story' and the Chancellor were removed. Size now shows WRNS's 266,000 sq ft and Rudolph and Sletten's 264,000; the roughly 1,500 occupants come from Rudolph and Sletten's page and the global health programs from UCSF's history page. Design-builder and landscape architect are now cited to their own project pages. The address note no longer says the architect's page gives 550 16th St (it gives no address), and the Wikimedia credit no longer names an author or a flight the file page does not state. The September 2014 occupancy and October 2014 ribbon-cutting rest on a UCSF page that could not be read and were left in place; their timeline rows now cite its URL instead of a bare domain.

column5: Corrected the Bayfront Medical Building's construction-start date, cost scope, Regents item wording and image credit to match sources.
column6: The construction start now reads September 2021, from Clark's September 23, 2021 groundbreaking release, instead of October 2, 2021, which is only the date of SF YIMBY's article. The $228 million figure no longer says it covers the building alone: Commercial Property Executive does not say whether it includes the garage. The May 2020 Regents milestone now says the committee's agenda lists the Block 34 items for action, since the outcome was not shown by a source read, and cites the agenda PDF. The summary now separates the building's address (520 Illinois St, per CPE) from the Block 34 corner of 3rd and Mariposa and no longer quotes a UCSF project name that no readable source gives. Address, size, story count, architect, contractor and opening date are cited to CPE, SF YIMBY and Clark because UCSF Real Estate's page could not be read. The Wikimedia credit no longer names a flight the file page does not state.

column5: Corrected the Uber towers' occupancy, lease, architect, completion and steel-schedule wording to match their sources.
column6: The record no longer says Uber has occupied both towers since January 2022 on a 20-year lease for about 4,000 employees, or that it leases the entire office component: The Real Deal (2025) says Uber and the Warriors each lease office space there, and SF Standard (2023) says Uber never occupied 1725 Third St and was marketing it for sublease. The steel-erection dates are now labelled as Mortenson's November 2017 schedule rather than recorded events, and the Alexandria supplemental is dated January 2018, when it was filed. The note that Uber 'never fully staffed' 1725 Third St now says 'never occupied', as SF Standard does.

column5: Corrected Channel Mission Bay's completion wording and Gus's Community Market row to match their sources.
column6: The summary and timeline now say the city's building permit for the 315-unit building is recorded complete on July 22, 2014 (DataSF), rather than that no source states a completion date, and note a completed permit is not an opening date. Developer, design firm and UDR are cited to their own pages. The Gus's Community Market changelog row no longer claims a deli, butcher counter or cafe or a Channel Mission Bay ground-floor location, which the CBS article does not state; Gus's own site now backs the 1101 4th St address and current operation. The Wikimedia credit no longer names a flight the file page does not state.

column5: Corrected Chase Center's cost, Uber tenancy, opening-event and Thrive City tenant wording to match their sources.
column6: The $1.3 billion alternate cost figure was removed because its cited source gives only $1.4 billion. The Uber claims (a January 2022 move-in, a 20-year lease, about 4,000 employees, the whole office component) were replaced by The Real Deal's 2025 report that Uber and the Warriors each lease office space. The opening milestone now says Metallica and the SF Symphony played the September 6, 2019 opening and the Warriors first played there on October 5, 2019, the Valkyries milestone is described as their May 16, 2025 debut as scheduled per the SF Chronicle, and the Blocks 29-30 and 'no construction as of February 2025' wording for the neighboring hotel proposal was removed. Before, it called it a UCSF parking structure designed by WRNS Studio, but Watry's own page names Watry as designer and lists the owner only as 'Developer'.
